candidates.excerpt: CMA CGM has announced higher Freight All Kinds (FAK) rates from Asia to the Mediterranean and North Africa. The new rates will apply from 19 to 31 October 2026. The rates cover shipments from all main Asian ports to Mediterranean ports within the listed regions. They apply to dry and reefer containers, out-of-gauge cargo and paying empty containers.

candidates.title: New rail service of port of Gothenburg with Asian and MENA markets
candidates.excerpt: The first train on a new rail service for Swedish timber producer Fiskarheden has departed from Malungsfors bound for the Port of Gothenburg, carrying sawn timber destined for markets in Asia, the Middle East and North Africa. The service departs every other Monday, carrying 44 forty-foot containers per departure, with capacity to expand if demand grows. Fiskarheden exports approximately 90 percent of its production, with sawn timber used across furniture, construction and concrete formwork applications. The new rail connection, developed by TFK Logistics, provides a cost-effective and flexible route to international shipping via Gothenburg and is open to other companies in the Dalarna region as well as Fiskarheden. CEO Joakim Limberg described the return to rail freight at the Port of Gothenburg as a positive development aligned with the company’s ambition to move as much inland freight as possible by rail. candidates.excerpt: Maersk has announced revised Intermodal Fuel Fee levels for truck transportation in Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro, Croatia, Serbia and Slovenia. The updated Export Fuel Surcharge and Import Fuel Surcharge levels will apply from 1 October 2026, based on the delivery date, and remain in force until further notice. The revised charges are: Maersk attributed the temporary adjustments to rising global energy prices and the impact of the Middle East security situation on fuel availability and inland transportation costs. According to the Danish carrier, the revised fees are intended to maintain service continuity, protect cargo flows and secure sufficient vendor capacity across its landside network.

candidates.excerpt: Union Pacific has deployed its first two battery-electric locomotives in Southern California, beginning a field-testing program intended to assess the technology’s reliability and operational fit in freight service. The two Wabtec FLXdrive locomotives are the first half of a four-unit order by Union Pacific (NYSE:UNP). The railroad said the remaining two battery-electric units are scheduled to arrive in October, completing a fleet that will operate in the greater Los Angeles area. Union Pacific plans to use the locomotives in switching and local-customer service, putting them through daily work in a busy railyard environment. The railroad said the tests will yield data on the units’ performance, reliability and operating capabilities. Metallic ores and metals surged 15.1%, followed by petroleum and petroleum products, 12.5%, and nonmetallic minerals such as sand and stone, 7%. Grain paused its long stretch of gains, down 7.7%, joined by losses in coal, 3.1%, and motor vehicles and parts, 0.8%. candidates.excerpt: A BNSF train carrying mixed freight caught fire during a burglary in Riverside, California, Thursday morning. The train was traveling from Los Angeles to Chicago, BNSF told FreightWaves. Firefighters found an open upper container burning on the moving double-stack train. Officials have not identified the items inside or reported any stolen cargo. Riverside dispatchers received the first report at 4:40 a.m. near Chicago Avenue. Early information placed the train heading west from downtown. Crews later located it moving east between Spruce and Columbia streets. Riverside Fire Department deployed 19 firefighters, four engines, one truck and a chief officer. Crews move train for access Access problems prevented crews from reaching the flames at their first location. Incident commanders directed railroad personnel to reposition the equipment farther east. candidates.excerpt: American Industrial Transport, Inc. (AITX) announced three executive leadership appointments it said will strengthen its leadership for the next phase of railcar solutions. The organization said Peter Appel will take the helm as the next Chief Executive Officer, while Tim Kubiak will join AITX as the president and Chief Operating Officer and Eric Eng will take the position of Chief Strategy Officers. The organization said the new leadership would help it advance its strategy to “deliver more integrated railcar solutions that help freight shippers navigate increasingly dynamic supply chain logistics.” Appel will lead that strategy. Since November 2025, he has served as AITX’s interim CEO. Prior to that, Appel spent 12 years as Managing Director, Head of Rail at ITE Management, overseeing the company’s rail platform and growing it into one of the largest railcar fleets in North America and Europe. candidates.title: Texmaco Rail & Engineering rallies on Rs 131-crore order win
candidates.excerpt: Texmaco Rail & Engineering rallies on Rs 131-crore order win Texmaco Rail & Engineering rose 5.07% to Rs 121.87 after the company announced orders worth a combined Rs 131.36 crore. The company received two domestic orders. Transport Corporation of India awarded a Rs 24.48-crore order for the manufacture, supply and commissioning of one rake of Type ACT-1 wagons along with one BVCM wagon. The order is to be executed within 16 weeks from the date of the letter of intent. Touax Texmaco Railcar Leasing awarded a Rs 106.88-crore order for the manufacture and supply of four rakes of BFNS22.9 wagons along with four BVCM wagons. The order is to be completed by 26 May 2027. Texmaco Rail & Engineering is one of the promoters of Touax Texmaco Railcar Leasing. The company said there is no conflict of interest and the transaction has been carried out on an arm's-length basis.
